hypotheses.persona: Hybrid working professional with office commute on Tuesdays
hypotheses.rationale: Day 10 (Thursday) shows no morning departure routine (no keys, phone at counter suggests home start). The stable 19:00-21:45 evening routine persists. The lack of office indicators on Thursday aligns with a hybrid model where Wed/Thu are remote, reinforcing the Day 9 evidence.

Still unlikely due to the rigid dinner cleanup timing (19:09-19:11 on Day 9, 18:25-21:45 on Day 10) which is atypical for students. The 'phone at counter' at 07:21 could be alarm/checking, but the structured evening suggests professional discipline.

The specific Tuesday commute (Day 8) remains the strongest counter-evidence. Without new evidence of a commute on other days, this remains the least probable, though the home-based days (Wed/Thu) are consistent with it.

selected_evidence: Day 10, 07:21 — phone at counter_k1 (morning home start, no keys leaving, supports WFH pattern)
Day 10, 07:25 — bowl at table_d1 (breakfast at home, consistent with Day 9 WFH routine)
Day 10, 18:25 — fork at table_d1 (dinner served, slightly earlier than Day 9's 19:09 cleanup, but within evening window)
Day 10, 21:45 — fork at cupboard_k1 (late cleanup, matches Day 9's 21:45 plate cleanup, indicating consistent late-night kitchen activity)
Day 10, 21:45 — plate at cupboard_k1 (confirms late-night kitchen usage, reinforcing the 'hybrid worker' wind-down routine)
notes: Thursday (Day 10) confirms the 'home-based' pattern seen on Wednesday (Day 9). No keys observed leaving in the morning. The dinner cleanup time shifted slightly earlier (18:25 vs 19:09) but the late-night kitchen activity (21:45) remains constant. This strengthens the 'Hybrid' hypothesis. Need to observe Friday (Day 11) to see if the pattern holds or if an office day returns. The 'Student' hypothesis is weakening due to the rigid evening structure.
